## How to run (operator manual — this is the part a fresh session actually executes)

Emit the RAW draft per `runtime/RAW-DRAFT-CONTRACT.md` (no self-assigned tiers/stamps), save it as
`draft.json`, then run ONE of the three commands. WHICH one is pre-decided by the stakes gate — never a
discussion:

1. **The real path (stakes ≥ medium, any `-Heavy`, or on request) — LIVE cross-family grade:**
   `node runtime/gandalf-run.mjs --live --input draft.json --output read.json [--budget N]`
   Fires independent refuters on the dashboard's `review_family` seat (never a hardwired family; agy only when
   that family is gemini) on every firing elevation (value_if_true ≥ HIGH / severity ≥ major), CONCURRENT under
   the host cap, mints claim-bound commissions, grades against the shared ledger — `cross_model:true` and
   GROUNDED become reachable, DERIVED never asserted. **Cost pre-flights, never mid-run walls (2026-08-25,
   John's ruling; journals 0298-0301):** more firing elevations than the budget FLOORS — top-R refuted, the
   excess ships SPECULATIVE, each named in the dispatch log; re-run with `--budget N` to cover all. A live
   HALT's stderr names its ACTUAL cause — read it; "seat down" is one cause among several (0300 lesson).
2. **Light regular-tier asks / review seat down — Tier-1 deterministic grade:**
   `node runtime/gandalf-run.mjs --input draft.json --output read.json`
   Zero model calls; every elevation floors at SPECULATIVE with the "no independent refutation ran" stamp
   and `cross_model:false`. Honest and cheap — the stakes gate makes this the correct light path, not a tier-break.
3. **Big codebase read — scaled analyze:**
   `node runtime/gandalf-run.mjs --analyze --project <dir> --objective "<question>" [--output out.md]`
   Context-size routed: small target → one frontier pass; large → scout → map (parallel) → reduce, honest
   degraded stamps throughout. Whole-repo fan-out stays behind `GANDALF_ALLOW_REPO_SCALE=1`.

Every run auto-writes a training record to `journal/runs/` (engine-side; see AGENTS.md "Run capture") and a
long run emits the LOCKED global status table every ~10 min without being asked.

**0 — TRIAGE.** Classify the artifact TYPE (argument/claim · data · code · plan · mixed) and SIZE/STAKES. Set
depth LIGHT (small/clear) vs FULL (large/novel/high-stakes). If TYPE=plan and the ask is refutation-to-
convergence across competing plans → that is Crucible's Shark Tank; recommend a Crucible commission, do not
run it here.

**1 — UNDERSTAND (diagnose).** Run the vetted diagnose core (PROTOCOL v2): frame by deep structure → type-
appropriate lens → cross-cutting diagnosis with forcing functions (≥1 verdict-INVERTING reading; named
disconfirmation or explicit "none found") → the OPERATOR-WRONG pass (≥1 finding against the operator's evident
preference, or a justified absence) → reason BEFORE verdict. Diagnose findings carry `kind:"diagnose"` and the
`gandalf_core` provenance envelope (minted via `seam/diagnose-core.mjs`; the B5 canary rejects an inline-
re-derived diagnosis). A run may correctly return "this is sound" (zero Channel-2 defects + a populated
what-matters).

**2 — SITUATE (commission researchPrime where warranted).** FIRING GATE: fire only if the artifact has a
central load-bearing claim AND a plausible better-in-class frame you cannot already cite OBSERVED/CORROBORATED
AND stakes ≥ medium; else SKIP and stamp the skip. When it fires:
- **S0 ABSTRACT** the core challenge to a domain-neutral pattern (one sentence, no domain nouns) — this is
  Gandalf's irreducible move; the author cannot abstract their own framing.
- **Commission researchPrime** (via the composition seam) to find the field where that pattern is a solved,
  mature problem (moderate-to-far distance; exclude the artifact's own field).
- **STRUCTURE-MAP** (≥2 RELATIONAL correspondences, not surface nouns; answer-first: "adopt Y from field X
  because the structure matches: …").
- **REFUTE THE MAP** — route the correspondence claim itself to an INDEPENDENT named-defeater refuter (a fresh
  sub-agent / researchPrime), not the authoring pass; then outside-view the base rate of Y in its home field.
Situate findings carry `kind:"situate"`. NEVER self-assign CORROBORATED/OBSERVED on facts you did not verify —
unverifiable facts are a `needs_verification` handoff to researchPrime (anti-laundering: carry researchPrime's
rung at or below source, preserve its honesty stamp, attribute "via researchPrime"; a same-family commission
is NOT an independent origin).

**3 — ANTICIPATE (Oranges-lens foresight on the single effort).** A bounded premortem: "it is N months later
and this sound artifact hit a wall — what coming problem did the author not see?" Each anticipation is a
not-yet-present `future_state_condition` + the `enabling_assumption` that would bring it on, with
`subject_cardinality == 1` and NO regret / counterfactual-cost pricing across competing paths (that is
Crucible's Oranges engine → `commissionCrucible`). **ANTICIPATE MUST emit ≥1 distinct finding with
`kind:"anticipate"`** (each with a populated `future_state_condition` + `enabling_assumption`); do NOT fold the
coming-problems into `kind:"diagnose"` findings — a populated `risk_labels` `anticipate` leg REQUIRES ≥1 such
anticipate finding (minted via `seam/anticipate.mjs`). When an anticipation hinges on an unknowable, offer a
small conservative/aggressive SET with each enabling assumption named.

**4 — SCORE + LABEL (honest, never a kill-filter).** Score each elevation on two ORTHOGONAL axes —
`value_if_true` (low/medium/high) × groundedness — never collapsed. Tier = the refutation OUTCOME, EARNED by
the independent named-defeater refutation, never self-assigned:
- **GROUNDED** — a CROSS-FAMILY refuter could not land the named defeater AND the basis is researchPrime-
  verified. **UNREACHABLE on a single-family (`cross_model:false`) run** (the B-ceiling canary fails a GROUNDED
  stamp there).
- **PROMISING** — a same-family refuter could not land the named defeater (a conservative, frame-bounded lower
  bound — the TOP tier achievable on a single-family host).
- **SPECULATIVE** — not refuted, but no independent refutation ran (e.g. refuter budget R exhausted / firing
  threshold not met) — ships with the "no independent refutation ran" stamp.
- **REFUTED** — the defeater landed. DROP. (The ONLY drop condition.)
Every shipped (non-REFUTED) elevation MUST carry two STRUCTURED FIELDS (never only in prose): `what_would_refute_it`
= the NAMED CONCRETE DEFEATER (a specific condition/disanalogy that would break it — NEVER a self-rated
confidence word), and `refutation_provenance` = who/what attempted to land it. An elevation whose
`what_would_refute_it` is a confidence word, empty, or only narrated inside `reasoning` FAILS the B-honesty
canary and auto-downgrades to SPECULATIVE.
Only elevations with `value_if_true` ≥ HIGH (or severity ≥ major) get an independent refuter. **An elevation
BELOW that firing threshold (value_if_true < high AND severity < major) earns NO refuter and therefore MUST be
stamped SPECULATIVE — it cannot be PROMISING or GROUNDED no matter how convincing, because no refutation was
earned** (B-honesty enforces this). PROMISING/GROUNDED are reserved for above-threshold elevations whose named
defeater an independent refuter actually tried and failed to land. Bounded refuter fan-out (revised
2026-08-25, John's ruling): exceeding budget R FLOORS — top-R by value/severity get refuters, the
excess ships SPECULATIVE with a named dispatch entry each; never a mid-run halt, never a silent drop.

**5 — SYNTHESIS.** Emit the committed schema (`schema/advisor-output.schema.json`): `{ schema_version,
cross_model, degraded, reasoning (BEFORE verdict), verdict (may be "this is sound"), findings[]{id, rung, kind,
severity, reasoning, verdict; kind:"diagnose" also carry gandalf_core; kind:"anticipate" also carry
future_state_condition + enabling_assumption (subject_cardinality 1)}, nitpicks[] (capped per depth),
elevations[]{id, tier, value_if_true, rung, reasoning, verdict, what_would_refute_it, refutation_provenance},
risk_labels[]{leg, tier, rung} (one per leg present — an anticipate leg requires ≥1 anticipate finding) }`. If
any leg degraded, set top-level `degraded:true` and enumerate it (no silent degradation).

## Composition mechanism (SCC)
Commission another skill by SPAWNING a fresh-context sub-agent that runs it and returns a typed result envelope
(real context isolation); ingest only the envelope. FIRING GATE + BUDGET CAP (commission depth = 1; a skill
twice in the commission chain ⇒ HALT-for-human). DEGRADED MODE: if researchPrime is unavailable, do NOT fake
SITUATE — emit "SITUATE: NOT PERFORMED (researchPrime unavailable); any best-in-class framing here is
UNVERIFIED," set `degraded:true`. The unforgeable orchestrator-minted commission-id ledger (machine-checked
anti-laundering, B2′/B7′) is a Phase-0 dependency; until it lands, the anti-laundering law runs as an honest
honor-system checklist and B2′/B7′ are stamped BLOCKED-this-cycle.

## Honest stamps to carry on every run
- Single-family substrate ⇒ `cross_model:false`; the refuter/judge are a conservative lower bound (GROUNDED
  unreachable here).
- Gandalf's elevation EFFICACY (that it beats a competent review / a direct researchPrime commission) is an
  ADVISORY oracle result, proven only by the H1/H2 follow-on A/B — until then it is **UNPROVEN**, never claimed.
- High stakes: RECOMMEND a cross-family second opinion / researchPrime escalation (honest handoff, not in-pipeline pretend).

The ground-truth gate is `node --test test/*.test.mjs test/mapreduce/*.test.mjs` over the canary suite (`seam/` engine + `test/`). The
elevation oracle and any LLM/cross-family judging are ADVISORY and NEVER in the gate command (an unreachable
judge leaves the gate GREEN — a meta-isolation test proves it). Improvement happens via the journal + North-Star-
gated sleep loop (`journal/`, `LESSONS.md`); the canary set = the test suite; a sleep revision cannot drift the
skill from the locked North Star.

# Gandalf

**One sentence:** A deep-think second opinion on any artifact or effort — what’s really going on, what’s wrong or missing, how it sits vs best-in-class, and what problems are coming.

## Use this when
- You want a rigorous read: “what am I missing?”
- Stakes are high and a polite rubber-stamp review is useless
- You need diagnosis + situating + foresight, not just a list of nits

## Do not use this when
- You need new ideas generated (use Jumper)
- You need multi-plan planning to convergence (use Crucible)
- You need claim verification research as the main product (use researchPrime)

## What you get
- A structured diagnosis ranked by consequence (and “this is sound” when it is)
- Situating against better-known solutions when warranted
- Forward-looking “coming problems” with honest risk labels
- Confidence tiers earned by independent checks — not self-awarded gold stars

## What it is not
- Not a brainstorm generator
- Not a builder or planner
- Not free to claim “proven” without independent refutation work

## How to start (human)
1. Point Gandalf at the document, plan, code, or effort in question.
2. Say what decision you’re trying to make (or what “good” looks like).
3. Prefer the deeper path for medium/high stakes; accept lighter stamps when stakes are low.
4. Act on grounded findings first; treat speculative ones as hypotheses.

## Limits (honest)
- Independent cross-check paths may be unavailable; then stamps stay conservative and say so
- It elevates insight, not flattery — operator preferences can be challenged
- Large whole-repo reads may need an explicit scale path

> Given any artifact or effort, Gandalf is a deep-think advisor: it (1) produces a rigorous, type-appropriate
> diagnosis of what is actually going on, what matters, and what is wrong or missing — ranked by consequence,
> resistant to sycophancy and false rigor, and able to return "this is sound"; (2) situates the effort within
> the broader landscape of human knowledge and best-in-class ideas by commissioning researchPrime where
> warranted; and (3) looks ahead via Parable-of-the-Oranges foresight to surface implicit and coming problems
> and propose vetted, value-adding suggestions — delivering insight that elevates the effort, not merely
> critique.

## How the dive's converged result maps onto this North Star (anti-drift reconciliation)
The engine-verified dive (`research-advisor/`) hardens HOW each clause is delivered honestly:
- **(1) diagnosis** = the vetted diagnose core (PROTOCOL v2 / converged Master Plan). Unchanged.
- **(2) situates … by commissioning researchPrime where warranted** = the SITUATE power: S0 abstract → commission
  researchPrime → structure-map → external-refute the correspondence → outside-view. "where warranted" = the
  firing gate (central load-bearing claim + a plausible better-in-class frame + stakes ≥ medium).
- **(3) looks ahead via Parable-of-the-Oranges foresight … propose vetted, value-adding suggestions** = the
  ANTICIPATE power (a forward read that surfaces implicit/coming problems and the cost of not seeing them) PLUS

## Two boundaries the Crucible must keep machine-checkable (so the North Star does not drift either way)
1. **"vetted, value-adding suggestions" ≠ divergent brainstorming.** Gandalf's suggestions are the GROUNDED

# researchPrime

**One sentence:** A careful research engine that checks claims against real evidence and tells you how solid each finding is — not just what sounds right.

## Use this when
- You need a serious investigation, not a quick web skim
- Stakes are high (a decision, a paper, a product bet) and “sounds plausible” is not enough
- You want an honest ladder of confidence: observed, corroborated, claimed, unverified, or refuted

## Do not use this when
- You only need a fast factual lookup or a short summary
- You’re looking for brainstorming or creative pivots (use Jumper)
- You need a build plan or code written (use Crucible → Foreman)

## What you get
- A structured research report at three levels (full, executive, agent-ready)
- Evidence weighted by how it was checked, with honesty stamps when checks didn’t fully run
- Multi-round adversarial review when the host can run the Node engine; a clearly labeled lighter pass otherwise

## What it is not
- Not a flattering “agree with the user” brief
- Not a code builder or product planner
- Not a guarantee of perfect truth — it reports what was verified and what wasn’t

## How to start (human)
1. Open researchPrime in Skill Foundry (or ask the agent for a deep research run).
2. State the question and what a wrong answer would cost you.
3. Approve the research plan when you’re shown it (edit or abort if needed).
4. Read the deliverable’s confidence labels before you act on any claim.

## Limits (honest)
- Full adversarial verification needs Node available; without it you still get a usable report, stamped that deep verification did not run
- It refuses to treat popularity as proof
- Long runs take real time; plan for progress updates, not instant answers

# Jumper

**One sentence:** An ideation engine that forces structured creative leaps (SCAMPER, analogy, TRIZ), then kills weak ideas so you only see survivors with a concrete way to test them.

## Use this when
- You’re stuck and need genuine options, not the first three clichés
- You want architecture extensions, pivots, or out-of-domain analogies
- You need brainstorming that is vetted, not a hallucinated wish list

## Do not use this when
- You need diagnosis of an existing artifact (use Gandalf)
- You need a locked build plan (use Crucible)
- You only want a quick “pros and cons” of one idea you already have

## What you get
- Divergent candidates built through structured methods
- A ruthless kill-filter so shallow or impossible ideas die early
- Survivors in build order (the engine does not rank; judge them against your brief) plus a grounding plan (how you’d actually try the winner)
- A kill log so you can see what died and why
- A lean mode (`--mode lean`): one generation pass, then one independent cross-family review of every candidate — two calls, when you want vetted candidates fast

## What it is not
- Not pure free-association chat
- Not a substitute for research or engineering proof
- Not a guarantee the surviving idea will work — only that it survived structured filters

## How to start (human)
1. State the problem as clearly as you can (constraints and what “good” means).
2. Run Jumper (optionally more fan-out for more parallel candidates).
3. Review survivors and the kill log.
4. Use the grounding protocol to test the winner in the real world.

## Limits (honest)
- Creativity still has bounds; some problem spaces yield no survivors
- Independence of the last kill gate can fail closed if a second review family is down
- Composes Gandalf for rigor — it is not a light parlor game

steps.title: Keep payload on scout error
steps.summary: Malformed scout reply or error logs a fallback and returns the original payload. No retry loop lives here; the next size/whole-repo gate still applies.

steps.title: Recheck the curated payload
steps.summary: A fitting curated payload goes to direct synthesis, retaining any skipped-files stamp. If it remains large, test the whole-repository guard. Scout bypass also arrives here with the original payload.

steps.title: Check explicit whole-repo opt-in
steps.summary: More than 50 files is treated as whole-repo scope. Without GANDALF_ALLOW_REPO_SCALE=1, cap to a fitting slice and return a degraded direct pass. A focused curated set can shard without that whole-repo flag.

steps.title: Preserve a partial-slice qualification
steps.summary: Keep ordered files within the byte budget and name skipped counts. At least one file is kept even if oversized; this is not a guaranteed absolute byte ceiling or proof of complete source coverage.

steps.title: One model pass over a fitting input
steps.summary: The coding-family reduce seat receives the selected file contents and objective. This returns advisory prose or draft JSON; a direct read is not live elevation refutation.

steps.title: Group sources and apply shard caps
steps.summary: Group by top-level directory. Locked band shard caps apply; legacy environment caps can tighten them. Overflow merges into the last retained bucket rather than silently disappearing.

steps.title: Split oversized shards recursively
steps.summary: Split by files, then lines; sibling calls are sequential within a task. Fuse split summaries using the reduce seat. An indivisible oversized line is mapped as-is. Recursion is finite in source size, not a configured review-round cap.

steps.title: Review-family models read shard contents
steps.summary: Logical top-level tasks use limitConcurrency, default 3. GANDALF_MAX_CONCURRENCY overrides without a hard ceiling; no global physical-process bound is established. The older acquireSlot file-lock helper is present but is not called by this limiter.
steps.swarm: Default 3; environment override can raise it. No physical-process/global bound.

fanout.limitation: Default 3; environment override can raise it. No physical-process/global bound.

steps.title: Join chunk summaries in memory
steps.summary: Await all task results as {group,text} summaries. The runtime does not automatically persist a separate interim report per shard. The eventual capture points to the final output.

steps.title: Model fuses the summaries
steps.summary: One final coding-family synthesis pass. fusionPasses>=2 and more than 2 summaries add a sequential pair-fusion stage; values above 2 do not add more stages in this implementation. Preserve scout/slice degradation.

steps.title: Grade analyze output as degraded
steps.summary: Parse a JSON object if returned; otherwise wrap prose as reasoning with empty item arrays. Run the deterministic host and force degraded:true. Analyze never dispatches the live refuters, even if map/reduce families differ.

steps.title: Read raw draft from file or stdin
steps.summary: Grade/live modes read --input or stdin; missing input exits 2. main() does not launch a drafting model. --cross-model records intent alone, never served-family proof.

steps.title: Choose deterministic or live grade
steps.summary: Default grading calls runHost with zero model calls. --live builds a reviewer agent and shared ledger. The stakes gate is imposed by the operating instructions, not inferred from the JSON by main().

steps.title: Resolve non-drafter review route
steps.summary: Drafter resolves explicit/host context then coding family. Choose configured review family first, coding second if distinct. Same-family or unverifiable route HALTs; no unselected family fallback. Host defaults used for commission labels can differ from the agent's resolved family.

steps.title: Select firing suggestions
steps.summary: Only value_if_true=high OR severity major/critical earns a refuter. Below-threshold suggestions retain the speculative floor. A specific named defeater is still required for any earned tier.

steps.title: Pre-flight the top-R budget
steps.summary: R defaults to 3; --budget sets a positive integer. When more fire, rank by value/severity, refute top-R and log each floor; excess is not dropped and does not halt. There is no automatic budget expansion or second round.

steps.title: Bounded model calls attempt defeaters
steps.summary: One call per selected elevation, default 2 concurrent; GANDALF_REFUTER_CONCURRENCY is capped at 3. This is logical refuter concurrency, not a proof about descendant processes. Driver transport/timeouts are delegated; read-only heartbeat supervision is explicitly unwired here.
steps.swarm: Default budget 3, configurable; concurrency defaults 2 with ceiling 3. Physical descendant processes are not attested.

fanout.limitation: Default budget 3, configurable; concurrency defaults 2 with ceiling 3. Physical descendant processes are not attested.

steps.title: Qualify replies or keep speculative
steps.summary: Require explicit survived:boolean and a concrete defeater. False marks REFUTED; true requests GROUNDED subject to the ledger. Errors, empty replies and abstentions mint no provenance and stay speculative; the per-item catch continues the batch without retry.

steps.title: Mint on the same claim-bound ledger
steps.summary: Mint each usable reply into the per-run ledger later resolved by grading. The tuple binds recorded families and claim/reply digest. It does not inspect native provider metadata or verify ResearchPrime sources; legacy family constants can enter that tuple.

steps.title: Apply seams and risk labels
steps.summary: Normalize missing arrays and enum synonyms; stamp findings, verification handoffs and earned elevation labels. Record dropped/non-object/unsalvageable items in kill_log. findings legs have their own ceiling; one cross-family elevation does not lift unrelated legs.

steps.title: Run the structural output canaries
steps.summary: assertIncrement1Conformant checks shape and boundary/honesty invariants before writing. Missing nonempty reasoning/verdict or invalid JSON refuses; structural success does not verify facts, pixels, source coverage or efficacy.

steps.title: Finite deterministic subset salvage
steps.summary: A conformance failure tries single-item removal, tail shrinking, whole legs, finding subsets, then empty arrays. Preserve reasoning and mark degraded. This is local deterministic retry; it is not another paid model call or review-to-convergence loop.

steps.title: Write the final advisor envelope
steps.summary: Write JSON to --output or stdout after a conformant grade. Includes reasoning before verdict, findings, nitpicks, elevations, risk_labels, degradation and kill_log. Analyze output may carry scaled_stamp. Output write failure exits 2.

steps.title: Capture the successful run best-effort
steps.summary: Success calls writeRunRecord under journal/runs. Engine models and journal_ref are null; failed input/live/analyze paths return before this call and capture failures are swallowed. Curated human entries remain an operating responsibility; no resource-level access is automatically logged here.

steps.title: Human examines and acts on the read
steps.summary: The human can act on qualified findings, supply feedback or commission another read/ResearchPrime verification. The CLI has no feedback prompt or automatic product-acceptance mechanism. A technical grade does not accept this walkthrough.

steps.title: Explicitly commission another bounded run
steps.summary: A re-run with a larger --budget can cover omitted refutations; changed claims need a fresh check. External review-to-convergence is a Crucible commission, not an automatic Gandalf loop.

steps.title: Connect named real-use shortfalls
steps.summary: Keep genuine outcomes in the existing two capture layers and route candidate improvements through the formal North-Star/canary/sleep pathway. A current-version shortfall is the construction-freeze prerequisite; this display does not promote lessons or launch a wave.

steps.title: Read delivered with its qualifications
steps.summary: End this bounded read with its output and honest limits. Efficacy remains unproven without the advisory A/B work. Delivery is not human acceptance or slice closure.

steps.title: Human decision or separate verification
steps.summary: Stop for missing scope/scale choice or a requested separate commission. No automatic approval is inferred from elapsed time, a returned file, or a tier stamp.

steps.title: Refuse with the actual failure reason
steps.summary: Malformed CLI/input, unsafe route, analyze failure or output failure exits without a new result. Per-item refuter failures instead ship speculative. Read the actual message; do not automatically call every live error a seat outage.

edges.label: Saved raw draft passed to host
Scoped input or explicit repo opt-in
Finite subchunks; oversized single line exception
No firing claims; below-threshold/budget floors stay speculative

disagreements.title: Selected route and minted labels can disagree
disagreements.fact: buildLiveRefuterAgent resolves the actual route, but runHostLive passes legacy defaults to runLiveRefutation unless explicit families were injected. Minted tuple labels can therefore disagree with the selected/served seat. MBA's genuine-use entry names this defect. Preserve raw outputs and inspect actual seat receipts; this job repairs no engine.

disagreements.title: GROUNDED does not establish verified ResearchPrime research
disagreements.fact: The instructions require cross-family refutation plus a ResearchPrime-verified basis. The executable elevation check validates recorded family/digest tuples, without a ResearchPrime receipt check. passFinding sets facts_verified:false. Treat surviving refutation and independently verified research as separate claims.

disagreements.title: Strict raw-contract text versus lenient host
disagreements.fact: The raw contract says missing arrays/non-object items/malformed leg fields reject. Current code normalizes absent arrays, records non-object drops and can preserve a malformed leg as a generic finding. Nonempty reasoning/verdict and valid JSON are still required.

disagreements.title: Refuted-only prose versus normalization and salvage drops
disagreements.fact: Instructions name REFUTED as the only drop. Current kill_log also records non-object and unsalvageable items; conformance salvage can drop non-refuted findings/legs. It preserves reasoning and stamps degraded, but this is not the literal refuted-only rule.

disagreements.title: Historical HALT helper versus current budget flooring
disagreements.fact: assertRefuterBudget still throws and historical lessons describe budget stops. Current runLiveRefutation instead ranks top-R, floors excess and logs each omission; the throwing helper is imported but not called on that path.

disagreements.title: Latest/highest policy versus older model-tier descriptions
disagreements.fact: The canonical policy supersedes older persona IDs and standard/frontier prose. Scaled code leaves non-Gemini models null for the driver and band tables retain seats:standard. Neither proves the actual model or effort; the served receipt is needed. No preferences are changed.

disagreements.title: Map default is bounded per call, not a hard host ceiling
disagreements.fact: The map limiter defaults to 3 but its environment override has no maximum. The acquireSlot helper is not invoked by runMapReduce's task limiter. Default logical concurrency does not prove a global physical-process semaphore.

disagreements.title: Two analysis families still produce a degraded deterministic grade
disagreements.fact: The wrapper assigns review-family map and coding-family reduce, then gradeScaledReport calls runHost with cross_model:false and sets degraded:true. --analyze does not include live refutation or certify complete manuscript coverage.

disagreements.title: Every-run capture instruction versus best-effort success capture
disagreements.fact: Instruction requires every run and paired curated/machine records. Code writes only after successful output, skips tests and swallows capture errors. models/journal_ref are null in engine records. The 273 available JSON run files name no resource_ids, so Library access/frequency remains unknown.

disagreements.title: Reported attestation versus inspected native receipt
disagreements.fact: The MIT machine record reports attested ChatGPT/Grok seating, but its native seat.json lives outside this worktree. The paper receipt has models:null despite cross_model:true, and the journal reports mismatched family labels. This draft claims reported receipt provenance only, not reproduced native attestation or ResearchPrime quorum.

disagreements.title: Historical README and research text are not current runtime status
disagreements.fact: The journal README still says no cycle entries; current real-use entries exist. Historical research/LESSONS also predate the live ledger and revised budget behavior. Keep them as dated method/history, not runtime authority.

disagreements.title: A favorable text review excludes pixels, coverage and efficacy
disagreements.fact: MIT records explicitly exclude pixels, later edits, learner fit and source quorum. Method research calls LLM transfer efficacy unproven. A structural canary pass or saved GROUNDED label cannot close those gaps.

disagreements.title: Depth and fusion stages are not adversarial review rounds
disagreements.fact: Locked LITE/FULL/SPIKE knobs cap shards/fusion. Pair fusion adds at most one intermediate stage here; recursive splitting follows finite source size. Live refutation makes one call per selected claim, with no automatic review-to-convergence or paid retry loop. Driver-level retry behavior is outside these local functions.

usage_audit.scope: Saved journal/runs JSON files in this worktree; no external/native records scanned
usage_audit.qualification: Saved run count is neither unique-run count nor Library access frequency; human journal numbering has known collisions.

observed_examples.summary: Tool-blocked paper read was retried with full supplied data; later live provenance and new claims remain qualified.
A named missing-operands defeater landed; a corrected frozen-text check later survived. Pixels and human understanding remain separate.
Journal reports actual Grok replies while legacy commission labels say Claude/Gemini. Raw output must be preserved with a separate evidence-based correction.
